title: No policy requires multi-factor authentication for privileged roles

messages.businessImpact: An administrator's password alone is enough to administer the tenant, which is the single most valuable credential an attacker can obtain here.
messages.technicalDetail: A policy counts when it is enabled, requires multi-factor authentication, and either names directory roles or targets all users. Naming the roles is the tidier way to write it, but a tenant that requires it of everyone has covered its administrators.
remediation: Create a policy targeting directory roles, or the group holding them, requiring multi-factor authentication.
Exclude emergency access accounts and protect them another way.
messages.cannotSee: Who a policy excludes is not resolved against the people holding privileged roles, so a policy over all users counts even where an excluded group happens to hold an administrator. Excluding the emergency access accounts is expected and does not change the answer.
